title: Plant reproduction
examples: What is the difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination?
How does the pollen actually get from one flower to another?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how plants make new life.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the parts of a flower. Look at the petal, the sepal and the anther. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The stamen has two parts, the anther and the filament.
The pistil has three main parts: the stigma, style, and ovary.
Pollination is when pollen moves from one flower to another.
Fertilisation happens when the pollen mixes with the ovule inside the ovary.

items: Step 1: Pollen grain lands on stigma
Step 2: Pollen tube grows down the style
Step 3: Nucleus fuses with ovule in ovary

explain.say: In real life, bees help plants by moving pollen between flowers.

faq.q: What is the main job of the anther?
faq.a: The anther is the part of the stamen that produces and holds the pollen grains. It is like the pollen factory of the flower.

faq.q: Does pollination always need an animal like a bee?
faq.a: No, wind and water can also carry pollen. Some plants are adapted to use these methods instead of animals.
asks: What if no insects are around?

faq.q: Where exactly does fertilisation take place?
faq.a: Fertilisation occurs inside the ovary, specifically when the pollen reaches the ovule. This fusion starts the seed development.
asks: Does fertilization happen in the stigma?

faq.q: What is the difference between pollination and fertilisation?
faq.a: Pollination is just the transfer of pollen to the stigma. Fertilisation is the actual fusion of the male and female reproductive cells inside the ovule.

faq.q: What is the role of the ovary after fertilisation?
faq.a: After fertilisation, the ovary develops into the fruit, and the ovules develop into the seeds. This helps protect the new plant.

facts: The stamen consists of the anther and the filament.
The stigma is sticky to catch airborne or carried pollen.
Cross-pollination involves pollen moving between different plants.
Fertilisation results in the development of seeds within the ovary.

quiz.say: The sticky top part of the pistil is called the:
quiz.why: The stigma is specifically designed to catch and receive pollen grains.

wrong.0: The anther produces the pollen, it does not receive it.
wrong.1: The ovary is deeper inside and holds the ovules, not the landing site.
wrong.2: The filament is just the stalk that supports the anther.

quiz.say: If wind carries pollen, this process is called:
quiz.why: Wind is a common agent that moves pollen from one plant to another.

wrong.0: Fertilisation is the joining of cells, not the movement of pollen.
wrong.1: This term refers to insects or animals carrying the pollen.
wrong.3: Self-pollination uses pollen from the same flower or plant.

quiz.say: Which sequence correctly shows the steps from pollen landing to seed formation?
quiz.why: Pollen lands on the stigma, grows down the style, and reaches the ovule.

wrong.1: This order mixes the pollen source with the receiving parts.
wrong.2: The style connects the stigma to the ovary where the ovule is located.
wrong.3: The anther is the source, not a step in the pollen's journey down the style.
